memory_lessons.applicability: T3 launch-geometry experiments on this target
memory_lessons.claim: The prior matched 128/128 grid-stride candidate passed all 11 correctness cases but measured 2.067 ms versus the baseline's 1.849 ms (score 0.472 versus 0.5). This does not isolate the cause, but the smaller matched launch geometry did not improve the measured result.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this 256-thread, 512-item tile candidate and compare its official geometric-mean result and correctness to the baseline; do not infer a speedup from the launch geometry alone.

proposal.hypothesis: With 256 threads per block and an items_per_block tile of 512, a grid-stride loop assigns up to two targets to each thread for larger inputs. Fewer threads and CTAs may reduce scheduling overhead, though the additional sequential target work per thread could instead hurt throughput. The pairwise arithmetic order and single-kernel interface remain unchanged; the controller must measure correctness and the prescribed geometric mean.

retained: Changed src/launch.json to use block=256, items_per_block=512, and no shared memory.
Changed target assignment to a grid-stride loop using a wide index so all outputs, including tails, are covered when the launch tile and block size differ.
Kept the pairwise force arithmetic and its iteration order unchanged; with the proposed tile, a thread may process two targets sequentially.
